exact_statement: For every Boolean F on at most six uniform physical bits with two distinguished address bits, whose positive conditional squared Fourier laws on the remaining bits are product laws, let w_J be the four address masses, N_J the number of conditional marginals outside {0,1/2,1}, and I_A=sum_J w_J |J|. Then Q=sum_J w_J N_J <= Kstar(H(w)+I_A), where Kstar=1/(45/8-(17 log2(17)+15 log2(5))/32)<1/2. This constant is attained by an actual six-bit Boolean truth table with w=(17,5,5,5)/32, all N_J=1 and I_A=5/8. Every individual admitted five-valued product-spectrum slice on four data bits has N_J<=1. No all-dimensional upper bound is asserted; the witness implies any all-dimensional constant must be at least Kstar.
hypotheses: F takes values +/-1 on the uniform physical cube
Two physical address coordinates; at most four data coordinates, dummy lifts permitted
Positive conditional spectral laws are coordinate products; omit zero rows
Entropy in bits; address influence uses the original physical labels
proof_dependencies: A032-TWO-ADDRESS-N6-CERTIFICATE@1: only its complete 45088-row catalogue and pointwise admission proof; pending external review
